title: Russian Missile Lands in Poland as Overnight Strikes Kill Nine Across Ukraine
excerpt: A suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in eastern Poland, prompting NATO scrambles, as Russia launched more than 70 missiles and 280 drones targeting cities from Kyiv to Lviv.
body:
• A Russian cruise missile landed in eastern Poland, creating a 33-foot crater near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia — the latest NATO airspace incursion linked to the war in Ukraine.
  • Russia launched over 70 missiles and approximately 280 drones in overnight attacks, killing at least nine people across Ukraine, including three children near Kryvyi Rih.
  • Ukraine's air defenses intercepted 55 missiles and 265 drones but shot down only one of nine ballistic missiles, exposing a critical Patriot shortage.
  • The EU disbursed $4 billion to Ukraine for defense procurement, while the U.S. Senate advanced the Lindsey Graham sanctions package targeting Russia.

Russia launched more than 70 missiles and roughly 280 drones at Ukraine in overnight attacks on Thursday, killing at least nine people and injuring dozens across the country. The barrage struck cities from Kyiv to the western city of Lviv, just 40 miles from the Polish border — and one missile crossed into NATO territory.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed that a Russian missile appeared to have come down in eastern Poland, landing in farmland near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia, just over 100 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. Authorities found a crater about 33 feet wide and scattered debris in an uninhabited area.

"All the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101, but we want to be 100% certain about the type of missile and who launched it."

— Donald Tusk, Polish Prime Minister

Deadly Toll Across Ukraine

The deadliest single strike hit a private home near Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine, where a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile killed six people, including two girls aged 5 and 12. Eight others were wounded. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi Rih's defense council, called it "a dark night" on Telegram. A day of mourning was declared for Friday.

https://x.com/ZelenskyyUa/status/2082706840081571877

A 31-year-old man was killed in Kyiv, where air raid alerts lasted over five hours and thousands sheltered in metro stations. One person each was killed in Lviv and Poltava. In Lviv, a missile struck a residential apartment building but did not explode. Emergency crews pulled survivors from beneath concrete slabs, with about 30 people including three children reported injured. More than 20 residential buildings, a school, and two kindergartens sustained damage.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also disclosed that Russia deployed a North Korean ballistic missile for the first time in nearly a year — preliminary data indicated the weapon was used in the strike on the village of Radushne in southeastern Ukraine that killed six.

NATO Scrambles as Missile Enters Poland

Poland's armed forces detected an unidentified object in its airspace at 3:40 a.m. local time. An F-16 was dispatched to intercept, but the object disappeared from radar minutes later. An Mi-24 helicopter later located the crash site. Tusk visited the location and said there was "no reason to think the target was Poland," adding that Ukrainian fighter pilots had attempted to shoot down missiles approaching the border.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called the incident "yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine." The U.S. expressed interest in joining the investigation. The incident is the latest in a string of airspace violations across NATO's eastern flank, including Romania and the Baltic states.

Air Defense Crisis

Ukraine's air force reported intercepting 55 missiles and 265 drones, but managed to shoot down only one of nine incoming ballistic missiles. Eleven missiles and 17 drones struck targets at 20 locations. The U.S.-made Patriot system — the only weapon in Ukraine's arsenal capable of reliably downing ballistic missiles — remains in chronically short supply globally.

"Untimely assistance and delays in the supply of anti-ballistic missiles result in the kind of destruction and casualties we are witnessing today."

— Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian President

Zelenskyy, returning from meetings in Washington with President Trump and the funeral of Sen. Lindsey Graham, said he had discussed licenses for Ukraine to produce Patriot interceptors domestically. European countries have offered to pay for additional U.S.-made interceptors.

Western Response Gains Momentum

Hours after the attack, the European Union disbursed $4 billion to Ukraine for defense procurement — including drones, missiles, air defense systems, and fighter jets — as part of a $100 billion loan approved earlier this year. The disbursement followed installments of $3.5 billion on June 25 and $4.5 billion on June 30.

In Washington, the U.S. Senate voted 84-12 to formally advance the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The package would impose sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, and financial institutions, and authorize tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas. Additional votes are required before final passage.

What's Next

Polish PM Tusk said the fate of the war could be decided within the next 100 days. His government is considering providing additional Patriot systems to Ukraine, despite recent strains in bilateral relations. The investigation into the missile that landed in Poland continues, with both Polish and potentially U.S. investigators working to confirm the weapon type and origin. For the millions of Indians living and working across Europe, the expanding geographic footprint of Russian strikes — now reaching NATO territory — adds a layer of security concern to an already volatile situation.
nri_angle: Expanding Russian strikes into NATO territory raise security concerns for the large Indian diaspora population across Europe.
